title: Help for Potential BTO Flat Owners Affected by COVID-19-related Construction Delays
what_it_is: Help for Potential BTO Flat Owners Affected by COVID-19-related Construction Delays

sections.label: BTO delays and supply questions
sections.summary: Questions asked whether BTO completion timelines will lengthen, whether affected flat owners get help, and whether more BTO flats will be built.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development in view of the constant start/stop in construction works with the surge in number of COVID-19 cases (a) whether the previous estimated timelines of HDB BTO project completions are expected to be lengthened; and (b) if so, whether further help will be given to the affected flat owners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development given the continued high demand for BTO flats coupled with the delay in completion of various ongoing BTO projects, whether the Ministry will consider bringing forward various planned BTO projects or consider building more BTO flats than currently planned.

sections.label: BTO flat supply increase
sections.summary: The Ministry adjusted supply, is on track to launch 17,000 BTO flats in 2021, and will launch more than 17,000 next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We recognise that demand for public housing has remained strong and that is why we had adjusted our supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We are on track to launch 17,000 BTO flats this year in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Next year, we will increase the BTO flat supply even further and launch more than 17,000 flats.

sections.label: Compensation for delayed BTO flats
sections.summary: Buyers facing delays beyond their Delivery Possession Date are compensated under COTMA, and waivers of forfeitures and wait-out periods will be considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Flat buyers who face delays that exceed their Delivery Possession Date, or DPD, will be compensated at the amount and for the period as set out in the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act, or COTMA, which applies to all developers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will also consider waiving flat booking forfeitures and the one-year wait-out period based on the flat buyers’ circumstances, such as for flat buyers who choose to cancel their BTO flats due to BTO delays and buy a resale flat to meet urgent housing needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Even amidst the ongoing pandemic, we are committed to delivering public housing to Singaporeans.

sections.label: More BTO flats for first-time buyers
sections.summary: More BTO flats will be pushed out next year and in future years, exceeding the more than 17,000 flats this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: These, of course, add on to the desire by people to have homes and exacerbated by this pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, for the first-time home buyers, we will be pushing out even more BTO flats next year and in future years, to ensure that their housing needs are met.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: As I have said earlier, we will push out more than 17,000 flats next year, more than what we have launched or are going to launch this year.

sections.label: PPHS targeting and income criteria
sections.summary: Moves in August targeted PPHS support to households with income below $7,000 and prioritised those with children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: To make sure that we target the PPHS supply to those who need such housing because of their limited housing options, we made some moves in August this year to target such support to those with household income of below $7,000 and prioritising those with children.

sections.label: Income ceiling review for applicants
sections.summary: Income ceilings were changed in recent years and household incomes of applicants continue to be reviewed to meet Singaporeans' needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Mr Seah Kian Peng mentioned earlier, if I can take this opportunity to address him, he did ask a question that I omitted to reply, which is with regard to the income ceiling as well as those who may feel that with a longer wait for housing, the risk of them busting the income ceiling is there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We have made some changes to income ceiling in the last few years and continue to review the household incomes of home applicants to ensure that it meets the needs of Singaporeans.
